title: 2005 AMC 10A Problem 14
statement: How many three-digit numbers satisfy the property that the middle digit is the average of the first and the last digits?

solutions.text:
The first and last digits must have the same parity so their average is a digit. Both odd gives \(5 \cdot 5 = 25\) pairs. Both even, with a nonzero leading digit, gives \(4 \cdot 5 = 20\) pairs. Each pair fixes the middle digit, for a total of \(25 + 20 = 45\) numbers.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The middle digit is an integer only when the first and last digits share the same parity
Count first-and-last digit pairs that are both odd or both even, remembering the first digit cannot be \(0\)
